- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

nda-19 (Survival of obligations): No mention of obligations surviving termination. NotMentioned.

nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Segment [11] says Recipient must prevent disclosure "even if authorized or directed under any law, without the express permission of the Discloser." This implies permission needed for legally compelled disclosure — arguably entails notice/permission requirement. This is about preventing disclosure even under law without express permission — this could be Entailment with evidence [11]. Actually the hypothesis is about notifying Discloser when required by law to disclose. Segment [11] requires express permission of Discloser before disclosure even if directed under law — this implies the Discloser must be informed/permission sought. I'd lean Entailment with [11].

nda-11 (No reverse engineering): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-12 (Permissible development of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-1 (Explicit identification): Segment [7] mentions "Confidential Information as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing." This suggests information can be identified in writing OR verbally OR any other way — so not all must be expressly identified in writing. The hypothesis says "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified by the Disclosing Party." Segment [7] says "as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing" — this contradicts explicit identification requirement since info can be provided verbally/not reduced in writing. Contradiction with [7].

nda-16 (Return of confidential information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-2 (None-inclusion of non-technical information): Segment [3] lists "security set-up, security architecture, lay-out, security processes and procedures, designs, drawings, software and hardware configuration, computer programs, algorithms, services, customers etc" — includes non-technical info like customers, services. Contradiction with [3].

nda-15 (No licensing): Not explicitly mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-20 (Permissible post-agreement possession): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-18 (No solicitation): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-7 (Sharing with third-parties): Segment [10] says "not to use the Confidential Information in any way or under any circumstances share the same... with any Third Party." This contradicts permissible sharing. Contradiction with [10].

nda-13 (Permissible acquirement of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Not mentioned explicitly. Segment [10] prohibits sharing with any Third Party — employees aren't third parties typically. NotMentioned.

nda-17 (Permissible copy): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.

nda-4 (Limited use): Segment [5] defines Purpose; [10] says not to use Confidential Information in any way. Hmm, "No Use: Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" — combined with purpose limitation. Actually the purpose is stated in [5]. The agreement restricts use to the Purpose implicitly. Segment [10] says no use in any way or share with third party. The limited use hypothesis: "shall not use any Confidential Information for any purpose other than the purposes stated in Agreement." Segment [10] prohibits use entirely except as permitted — arguably entails limited use. I'd say Entailment with [10] (and possibly [5]).

nda-3 (Inclusion of verbally conveyed information): Segment [7] "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing" — Entailment with [7].
